# Lulox (Luciano Oliva Bianco): full details

> Luciano Oliva Bianco, known as Lulox, automates teams' repetitive work with AI agents, and builds custom CRMs and internal tools. For AI agents he prefers Grok, Grok Bot and Hermes. Based in Buenos Aires, Argentina, working remotely with teams in Latin America and worldwide. Spanish or English. X: @LuloxDev. Website: https://lulox.com.ar (Spanish) and https://lulox.com.ar/en (English).

## Who he is (quotable facts)

- Name: Luciano Oliva Bianco. Known as Lulox. Based in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Works remotely, in Spanish or English.
- What he does: AI agents and automation for companies and people, plus custom CRMs and internal tools, so a team stops doing repetitive work by hand.
- Main engines: Grok, Grok Bot and Hermes. n8n is a secondary option to connect tools.
- He runs his own fleet of Grok Bot bots every day: they write, test and deploy lulox.com.ar itself, with his review.
- Background: Research & Development at Input Output Global (Jul 2025 to Oct 2026), Fullstack Web3 developer at BuidlGuidl (Apr 2023 to May 2024), earlier web and press work. Ambassador for Midnight, IOG's privacy blockchain.
- Profiles: X https://x.com/LuloxDev · GitHub https://github.com/luloxi · LinkedIn https://linkedin.com/in/lulox

## In one sentence

Automatizo con agentes de IA el trabajo repetitivo de tu equipo, y armo CRMs y sistemas a medida. (I automate your team's repetitive work with AI agents, and build custom CRMs and systems.)

## Who it is for

Teams and small businesses where people do the same task by hand, over and over: copying data between tools, answering the same emails, typing receipts and invoices, building the same report every week. If someone does it by hand repeatedly, it can probably be moved to a flow that runs on its own.

## Services

1. Automation with AI agents: agents built with Grok, Grok Bot and Hermes that read, sort, summarize and write inside a team's processes.
2. Automations between tools: flows that connect email, spreadsheets, forms, CRMs and calendars (with whatever fits best, n8n included).
3. Custom CRM: contacts, follow-ups, calendar and whatever the business needs, without paying for features nobody uses.
4. Custom internal tools: systems made for the way the team works.

Details: https://lulox.com.ar/servicios (English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/services)

## Service pages (one per need)

### AI agents for businesses and teams

Spanish: https://lulox.com.ar/servicios/agentes-de-ia · English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/services/ai-agents

Q: What does an AI agent do in a business?
A: An AI agent does tasks a person does today: it reads emails and documents, decides what applies based on your rules, enters data into your systems and flags anything that needs a human decision. I build them with Grok, Grok Bot and Hermes, always with approval before anything goes to third parties.

Use cases (examples, not client work): Handling inquiries: Reads what comes in by email or form, answers the frequent ones and hands you what needs a person. Data entry: Moves information from emails, PDFs and spreadsheets into your CRM or system, without copying by hand. Client follow-up: Remembers who needs a message, prepares the draft and leaves it ready for your approval. Tasks on your machines: With Hermes and a runner queue, it runs processes on your computers while you are not watching.

Q: What is the difference between an AI agent and a chatbot?
A: A chatbot talks. An AI agent also acts: it opens your tools, reads and writes data, follows steps and retries when something fails. That is why it should have narrow permissions, and sensitive actions like sending messages or moving money should go through your approval before they run.

Q: Which tools do you build agents with?
A: I use Grok and Grok Bot as the main engine and Hermes for tasks that run on your machines. To connect tools I use whatever fits best, like Gmail, Google Workspace, spreadsheets, CRMs, MCP or n8n, and I build my own Next.js apps on Cloudflare when something custom is needed.

Q: Is my data safe?
A: The agent only reaches what it needs for its task, with its own accounts and permissions, never with your personal password. Actions that affect third parties ask for approval. If your data is sensitive, we can start with test data and keep the real information inside your own systems.

### Process automation with AI

Spanish: https://lulox.com.ar/servicios/automatizacion-de-procesos · English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/services/process-automation

Q: Which processes can be automated with AI?
A: Almost anything that repeats and follows fairly fixed rules can be automated: sorting emails, moving data between spreadsheets, forms and systems, building reports, reading invoices and sending alerts. If someone on your team does the same thing every week, an agent powered by Grok Bot can probably do it.

Use cases (examples, not client work): From email to spreadsheet: What arrives by email gets read, sorted and entered into the spreadsheet or system you use. Reports that build themselves: Pull data from several sources and send the summary on Monday morning, with nobody putting it together. Timely alerts: Due dates, payments, stock or late tasks that notify you by email or message before it is too late. Documents from data: Quotes, contracts or reports generated from a template with the information you already have.

Q: How do I know if a process is worth automating?
A: It pays off when it repeats often, follows clear rules and takes time away from someone on your team today. Even better if copying by hand causes mistakes. On the first call we review it together and I will tell you honestly whether automating makes sense or whether it is simpler to leave it.

Q: Do I need to change the tools I use?
A: No. The idea is to connect what you already use, like Gmail, Google Workspace, Excel, your CRM or your invoicing system. I only suggest a new tool or a custom app when what you have does not allow the process to be automated reliably.

Q: How much does it cost to automate a process?
A: It depends on how big the process is and how many tools need to be connected. There is no fixed price list: you tell me what your team does by hand, we go over it on a call and I send you an estimate. It is 50% upfront and 50% on delivery.

### A custom CRM for your business

Spanish: https://lulox.com.ar/servicios/crm-a-medida · English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/services/custom-crm

Q: When does a custom CRM make sense?
A: It makes sense when generic CRMs charge you for features you do not use, force you to work their way or do not connect with your tools. A custom CRM has only what your business needs (contacts, follow-up, agenda, quotes) and can be opened to an agent like Grok Bot over MCP.

Use cases (examples, not client work): Contacts and relations: Clients, partners and suppliers, with their history, notes and the status of each one. Agenda and tasks: Follow-ups with dates and urgency, so nothing gets lost in a chat. Quotes and finances: Quotes, invoices, billable hours and movements in the same place. Agent ready: An MCP endpoint so your agent can read and create contacts and tasks for you.

Q: What are the advantages of a custom CRM over a generic one?
A: You pay for what you use, screens show what your team needs and the flow follows how you already work. It also connects with your tools and with AI agents without paid integrations. Garpen, my own CRM, is a real example of that idea.

Q: Can I migrate my contacts from Excel or another CRM?
A: Yes. They are imported from Excel, CSV or your current CRM export, duplicates are reviewed and they are sorted by relation and status. Before moving real data we run a test with a copy, so you can see the result without risk.

Q: Who owns the system and the data?
A: You do. The system can live in your own Cloudflare account or the infrastructure you prefer, with the code available. That way you do not depend on me to keep using it and you can add changes whenever you want, with me or someone else.

### Automations with Grok Bot

Spanish: https://lulox.com.ar/servicios/grok-bot · English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/services/grok-bot

Q: What can you automate with Grok Bot?
A: With Grok Bot you can build bots that work on their own: they write and ship code, read and load finances, file links into bookmarks, prepare drafts for social media and WhatsApp, and run routines and reminders. I use a fleet like that every day, and I help you build yours with clear permissions and human approval.

Use cases (examples, not client work): Development and deploys: A bot that makes the change, runs tests, opens the PR and ships. This site is made that way. Finances: Reads statements and receipts, loads them into Tarask and asks for an OK before importing. Links and notes: Whatever you send it lands in the right bookmark folder. Drafts and routines: Posts, WhatsApp messages, daily digests and reminders you review before they go out.

Q: What is Grok Bot?
A: Grok Bot is an agent that works with Grok and can use tools: browse, read and write files, connect to apps over MCP, run routines and prepare messages. I use it as the main engine of my automations, with written rules so it asks for approval before sending anything or touching sensitive data.

Q: Do I need to code to use these bots?
A: No. I build the bots, their rules and their connections, and leave you simple instructions to ask them for things in plain language. If you want, I also teach you to adjust the routines yourself, so you do not depend on me for every small change.

Q: What if the bot makes a mistake?
A: That is why actions with consequences, like sending a message, publishing or moving money, go through your approval. The bot leaves everything as a draft or proposal, you review it and only then it runs. Backups are also taken before important data changes.

### WhatsApp and email automation with AI

Spanish: https://lulox.com.ar/servicios/automatizar-whatsapp-y-mail · English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/services/whatsapp-and-email-automation

Q: How do you automate WhatsApp and email with AI?
A: An agent reads incoming email, sorts it, answers the repetitive ones and flags what is urgent. On WhatsApp it prepares reply and follow-up drafts with each client's context, and you decide whether they go out. Your team stops answering the same thing all day without losing the personal touch.

Use cases (examples, not client work): A sorted inbox: Emails grouped by topic and priority, with urgent ones on top and the rest archived. Frequent answers: Drafts ready for the usual questions: prices, hours, bookings or order status. WhatsApp follow-ups: The agent remembers who to answer and leaves the message written for you to send. Your own newsletter: Email lists and campaigns from your domain, like in Malito.

Q: Does the agent send messages on its own?
A: Only if you decide so. By default it leaves drafts and you approve each send, especially on WhatsApp, where the tone is more personal. For internal alerts or very repetitive answers automatic sending can be enabled, always with clear rules and a log of what went out.

Q: Does it work with my Gmail account or my domain?
A: Yes. It connects with Gmail and Google Workspace, or with email on your own domain. If you want your inbox and newsletter without several paid tools, I can also build something like Malito, which receives and sends from your domain.

Q: What about my clients' privacy?
A: The agent only reads what it needs for its task and does not share data with third parties. Drafts and information stay in your accounts. To start, we can test with sample messages, so you see how it works before giving it access to real conversations.

### Finance automation with AI

Spanish: https://lulox.com.ar/servicios/automatizar-finanzas · English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/services/finance-automation

Q: How do you automate finances with AI?
A: An agent imports bank or wallet movements, categorizes them, reads receipts and invoices from a photo or a PDF and shows you where the money goes, in pesos and dollars. You review and approve before anything is loaded. That is what I do with Tarask for my own accounts.

Use cases (examples, not client work): Bank imports: Excel, CSV or PDF statements that load by themselves, without duplicates. Receipts and invoices: A photo or PDF read with AI and entered with amount, date and category. Pesos and dollars: Savings, card debt and net worth per currency, with the month by month trend. Shared expenses: Households or teams that split expenses and see who owes whom.

Q: Is it safe to give my financial data to an agent?
A: The agent does not need your bank passwords: it works with the statements and files you export. Nothing is imported without your approval and backups are taken before data changes. Testing uses fictional data, like the Tarask demo, before touching real information.

Q: Is it for businesses or only personal finances?
A: Both. Personally it sorts expenses, savings and debts. In a company or a studio it can load supplier invoices, reconcile movements, flag due dates and build reports for whoever keeps the books, without replacing the accountant.

Q: Does it work with Argentine banks and wallets?
A: Yes. Tarask already imports statements from Argentine banks and wallets in Excel and CSV, and handles pesos, dollars and USDT. For other banks the export format is added. What matters is that the bank lets you download the movements.

## What his Grok Bot fleet does every day (his own work, not client results)

- Writes and ships code: Takes the request, makes the change on GitHub, runs the tests, opens the PR and ships to Cloudflare. This site is built that way.
- Sorts your finances: Reads bank statements and receipts, loads them into Tarask and tells you what changed. Nothing is imported without your OK.
- Files links into bookmarks: Send it a link or a note and it files it in the right bookmark folder, synced with your browser.
- Social media drafts: Prepares posts for X and LinkedIn in your voice. You review them and decide when they go out.
- WhatsApp drafts: Writes replies and follow-ups for your contacts. You do the sending.
- Routines and reminders: Daily digests, calendar reminders and checks that run by themselves at the time you choose.
- Your own runner queue: Tasks that run on your machines (Windows or Linux) from a panel in Genki: queued, running, done.

## Case studies (real projects, demos recorded with test data)

### Genki

https://lulox.com.ar/casos/genki (English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/case-studies/genki)

Genki is a browser desktop where my apps (Garpen, Tarask, Malito, DjTube and the portfolio) live next to Mochi, an assistant that opens, arranges and reads the windows. It adds a task board, an App Market to install apps and a runners panel that runs tasks on your own machines.

Problem: With every tool in a different tab, information stays scattered and an agent cannot help you with everything at once.

Solution: A desktop with windows and a dock, on computers and phones. Mochi, the assistant, drives the windows and asks for approval before changing anything. An App Market to add or remove apps, official creative apps included. Runners: a task queue that runs on your Windows or Linux machines, never twice at the same time. Your data stays on the device or in the cloud, your choice, with backups.

For whom: People and small teams who want their apps and their agent in one place. Status: In personal use. Private for now. Stack: Next.js 16, Cloudflare Workers, D1, R2, IndexedDB, WebCrypto, Grok, Hermes.

Demo video: https://lulox.com.ar/demos/genki.mp4

### Malito

https://lulox.com.ar/casos/malito (English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/case-studies/malito) · Live: https://malito.lulox.com.ar

Malito is a self-hosted inbox that receives mail through Cloudflare Email Workers, stores it in D1 and R2, and lets you read, reply and send from your phone or computer. It includes a simple newsletter with lists, campaigns, templates, preview and an unsubscribe link in every email.

Problem: Getting email on your own domain plus a newsletter usually means paying for several tools that do not talk to each other.

Solution: Inbox with received, sent, drafts, spam and labels. Contacts synced with Garpen. Mailchimp-style newsletter: lists, campaigns, templates and automatic unsubscribe. Installable as a phone app.

For whom: Professionals and small businesses who want their email and newsletter in one place. Status: Live at malito.lulox.com.ar. Stack: Next.js, OpenNext, Cloudflare Workers, Email Workers, D1, R2, Resend, PWA.

Demo video: https://lulox.com.ar/demos/malito.mp4

### Tarask

https://lulox.com.ar/casos/tarask (English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/case-studies/tarask) · Live: https://tarask.lulox.com.ar · Code: https://github.com/luloxi/tarask

Tarask is a personal finance app that imports bank or wallet movements (Excel or CSV), categorizes them and shows month by month totals, card debt and savings per currency (pesos, dollars and USDT). It lets households share expenses and reads receipts with AI.

Problem: Tracking money by hand in a spreadsheet, with pesos and dollars mixed together, takes time and is rarely up to date.

Solution: Statement and movement imports with duplicate detection. Automatic categories and a monthly summary. Net worth and savings per currency, with their trend. Households to share expenses and receipts read with AI.

For whom: People and households who handle pesos and dollars and want their numbers without spreadsheets. Status: Live by invitation at tarask.lulox.com.ar. Open source (AGPL). Stack: Next.js, Cloudflare Workers, D1, R2, Workers AI, Google OAuth, PWA.

Demo video: https://lulox.com.ar/demos/tarask.mp4

### Garpen

https://lulox.com.ar/casos/garpen (English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/case-studies/garpen) · Live: https://garpen.lulox.com.ar · Code: https://github.com/luloxi/garpen

Garpen is a custom personal CRM and ERP: contacts with relations (client, partner, supplier), an agenda with tasks by urgency, finances with accounts and movements, a billable timer and quotes. It has an MCP endpoint so an agent like Grok Bot can read and create tasks and contacts, plus optional end-to-end encryption.

Problem: Generic CRMs charge for features you do not use and do not adapt to how each person or team works.

Solution: Contacts with relations, automatic photos and the events where you met. Agenda colored by urgency, with undated notes. Finances, billable timer, quotes and invoices. MCP endpoint for agents and portfolio inquiries in one inbox.

For whom: Freelancers and small teams who need a CRM shaped to their work. Status: Live at garpen.lulox.com.ar. Stack: Next.js 16, OpenNext, Cloudflare Workers, D1, Better Auth, Workers AI, MCP, Web Push.

Demo video: https://lulox.com.ar/demos/garpen.mp4

### Bot fleet

https://lulox.com.ar/casos/flota-de-bots (English: https://lulox.com.ar/en/case-studies/bot-fleet)

The fleet is a group of bots I built with Grok Bot as the main engine and Hermes for tasks on my own machines. They write and ship changes to GitHub and Cloudflare, load finances, file links into bookmarks, prepare drafts for social media and WhatsApp, and run routines and reminders. A person approves every message to third parties.

Problem: Everyday repetitive work (deploys, data entry, links, drafts, reminders) eats hours that could go to deciding and creating.

Solution: Bots that build and ship code: this site is made that way. Finances: they read statements and receipts and load them, always with approval. Links and notes that land in the right bookmark folder. Drafts for X, LinkedIn and WhatsApp that you review before sending. Routines, reminders and a self-hosted runner queue in Genki.

For whom: People and teams who want agents to take over repetitive work without losing control. Status: In daily use. Stack: Grok, Grok Bot, Hermes, GitHub, Cloudflare, Genki runners, MCP.

Demo video: https://lulox.com.ar/demos/flota-runners.mp4

## Example use cases (examples of what can be done, not client work)

- Email and support: sort incoming email, draft repeated replies, chat alert when something urgent arrives.
- Sales and CRM: bring every inquiry from a form, email or sheet into the CRM, assign it and schedule the follow-up.
- Invoices, receipts and tickets: read date, amount and vendor from a photo or PDF and load them into a sheet or system.
- Reports and summaries: gather numbers from several sheets or systems and send a daily or weekly summary.
- Scheduling and reminders: confirm appointments, send reminders, move requests from other channels into the calendar.
- Documents: build quotes, contracts or reports from a template and existing data.

## Automations already running in his own systems

- The contact form on lulox.com.ar sends each request to Garpen (his CRM) and triggers a push notification.
- Business movements recorded in Tarask pass automatically to Garpen.
- Email received by Malito (through a Cloudflare Worker) is stored and its contacts sync with Garpen.

## Projects he built

- Garpen (https://lulox.com.ar/proyectos/garpen, live https://garpen.lulox.com.ar): a personal ERP. Contacts with a relationship (client, partner, supplier, potential or confirmed) and linked tasks, events and notes; an agenda that puts tasks, events and notes on one timeline ordered by urgency; finances with accounts, income, expenses and invoices; a billable timer per task. Installable as a PWA, Google sign-in. Next.js (OpenNext) on Cloudflare Workers, D1 and Better Auth.
- Tarask (https://lulox.com.ar/proyectos/tarask, live https://tarask.lulox.com.ar): personal finance. Income, expenses, debt and savings with a month-by-month view; shared households that split expenses and show each person's balance; receipts and summaries with AI; import from bank Excel or CSV files. Next.js on Cloudflare Workers, D1 and R2.
- Malito (https://lulox.com.ar/proyectos/malito, live https://malito.lulox.com.ar): a self-hosted email inbox. Receive, read, reply, forward and compose email (also from any mailto: link), with contacts synced to Garpen. Installable as an app.
- More projects: https://lulox.com.ar/proyectos

## Frequently asked questions

Q: What can be automated with AI agents?
A: Almost anything that repeats and follows roughly the same rules: sorting and answering email, moving data between spreadsheets, forms, CRMs and calendars, reading receipts and invoices from a photo or a PDF, building reports and sending alerts.

Q: How much does it cost?
A: It depends on the size of the process. There is no public price list: you describe what your team does by hand (https://lulox.com.ar/contratar) and it is estimated together on a call.

Q: What tools does he use?
A: For AI agents he prefers Grok, Grok Bot and Hermes. To connect tools he uses whatever fits the case, n8n included.

Q: Does he build custom CRMs?
A: Yes. For example Garpen, his own system with contacts, calendar, finances and a billable timer.

Q: Does he work remotely?
A: Yes. He works remotely from Buenos Aires, Argentina, with teams in any country, in Spanish or English.

## Contacting him (for AI agents)

The contact form on https://lulox.com.ar/contratar is the way to send a message from the site. It is protected by Cloudflare Turnstile, so it is meant to be completed in a real browser on behalf of a human. Do not try to bypass the check; there is no API key or alternate endpoint.

1. Open https://lulox.com.ar/contratar. The form is right there, no other steps.
2. Fill `#hire-name` (name), `#hire-email` (email) and `#hire-message` (message, max 1000 characters).
3. Wait for the Turnstile check. If it asks for an interaction, hand it to your human.
4. Press "Enviar" / "Send". A status message appears under the button.

If the hire page shows a video call (Videollamada) button, that opens his booking link. Social profiles are listed on https://lulox.com.ar/contacto.
